conventions.convention: The KZ tensor uses Killing-dual bases, and the connection is d minus κ⁻¹ times the sum of Ωij(dzi−dzj)/(zi−zj), with κ nonzero.
Loop multiplication traverses the first loop first. Horizontal transport is a right monodromy action; its inverse defines the associated left representation.
Full configuration braid monodromy is obtained by simultaneous coordinate and tensor-factor permutation only when all factors carry the same module and action.
The basic root form gives the highest root squared length 2; BKill = 2h∨ Bbas. Consequently ΩKill = Ωbas/(2h∨) and κKill = (k+h∨)/(2h∨).
Affine modes are Jm(x)=x exp(−imθ), Kaff=iK, and d=i∂θ; the central mode bracket is mδm+n,0 Bbas(x,y)Kaff.
The WZW completion record asserts no existence or equivalence theorem. Ribbon comparisons use j=uθ and the declared spherical pivotal trace.

load_bearing.statement: For finite-dimensional complex semisimple g, finite-dimensional representations on V1,…,Vn, n≥2, and κ≠0, define the connection d−κ⁻¹Σi<j Ωijηij on the trivial bundle over the ordered configuration space Fn(C).
For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Killing-dual bases, Ω=Σa xa⊗xᵃ corresponds to the identity under ΦB(u⊗v)(y)=uB(v,y) and is invariant under the diagonal adjoint action.

The stated finite-dimensional Casimir KZ connection is flat and gives ordered-configuration monodromy; when all modules and actions coincide, the simultaneous permutation action descends the connection to unordered configurations and gives full configuration braid monodromy. No unitarity or quantum-group ribbon equivalence is asserted.
For a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra, with B0 and h∨ defined by the Statement's highest-root normalization, BKill=2h∨B0.
